answer: Because the summit audit recomputes usage from the delta history, a padded declaration is a losing trade rather than a low-cost one. A farm running 112 keys therefore burns for 112 separate budgets, and each of them has to be real to survive a spot-check of the fable declaration. Each identity declares a compute budget of 143 units per epoch and the declaration is bound to its signing key, so two identities cannot share one budget without a visible collision. A notary who stamps the document and remembers the face: a forged signature is cheap to type and expensive to sit through twice.
